decisions.title: Clarify P1-010 processing-cost allocation contract
decisions.scope: Supplemental forward-only contract clarification for closed P1-010 only. Processing-cost allocation uses the existing policy, immutable Fee Calculation snapshot, frozen Payment Transaction provenance, append-only Ledger, reconciliation, and provider-adapter boundaries. No schema, migration, database, Payout, G-1 through G-5, jurisdiction-specific production economics, provider-specific economics, or P1-012 change is authorized.
decisions.decision: Processing-cost economics are jurisdiction/policy-driven and payment-provider-neutral. The applicable approved versioned financial policy may allocate processing cost to the attorney, Rosuno, the client, split it among parties, or use another future approved allocation; no universal processing-cost bearer is established. The immutable Fee Calculation calculation_snapshot must preserve enough provider-neutral information to reconstruct the processing-cost economic treatment that applied, including relevant policy/pricing provenance and resulting client, attorney, and Rosuno economic effects. This clarification defines no exact JSON property vocabulary or object shape. Frozen transaction policy provenance preserves historical economics, and later Policy Versions cannot retroactively alter earlier transaction economics. Actual provider processing costs and variances belong to append-only Ledger and reconciliation history rather than rewriting the original Fee Calculation. Payment-provider adapters execute approved economics and report provider observations; they do not define Rosuno economics.
decisions.rationale: The locked financial authority already requires independent processing-cost calculation, versioned policy provenance, immutable Fee Calculations, provider isolation, append-only Ledger history, and reconciliation. The existing physical model therefore already has the required capability through calculation_snapshot, frozen Payment Transaction policy references, generic Ledger entries, and Reconciliation Exceptions. This supplemental decision makes that existing capability explicit and testable without inventing schema or a processing-cost JSON vocabulary.
decisions.impact: Adds governance/test protection for the existing P1-010 processing-cost capability only. Historical P1-010 migration bytes and the original P1-010 decision, work item, release, closure evidence, migration registry, baseline, controls.mjs, contract-data, Staging, Production, OLD, Payout boundary, G-1 through G-5, and P1-012 remain unchanged. decisions.title: Register bounded P2-003 Security Shell contract
decisions.scope: Governance registration only for Implementation Master Plan P2/2C Security Shell. Records the smallest generic server-side application security contract for authenticated-route protection, principal-context resolution, capability checks, server-side mutation authorization boundaries, and error redaction inside the existing apps/web application. No P2-003 application implementation, P3 identity/authentication workflow, database/RLS/provider integration, feature-specific authorization, jurisdiction-specific implementation, environment mutation, publication, review, merge, or later work is authorized by this decision.
decisions.decision: Register WI-P2-003-SECURITY-SHELL as the bounded P2/2C Security Shell slice after completed P2-001 and P2-002. P2-003 may later implement only generic server-side security primitives: fail-closed protected-route decisions based on trusted server-derived session state; principal contexts for client, attorney, and staff without treating them as one mutable browser-supplied role; exact capability and scope requirements evaluated through trusted server-side authorization inputs; a mutation guard that authorizes before invoking a server-side mutation; and presentation-safe redacted failure results. Browser input may never authoritatively assert identity, principal context, role, capability, scope, or authorization. No universal admin, superuser, wildcard, or everything capability is permitted. Resource-specific ownership, relationship, business-rule, policy, and jurisdiction authorization remains the responsibility of later owning workflows and must not be invented inside this generic shell. P3 remains responsible for actual account creation, sign-in, sign-out, recovery, verification, profile lifecycle, real identity-provider integration, session binding, RLS integration, rate limiting, abuse controls, suspicious-login handling, and stronger authentication.
decisions.rationale: The locked Implementation Master Plan orders P2 as 2A Application Shell, 2B Design System, then 2C Security Shell. P2-001 already provides a server-owned anonymous/authenticated session representation and explicit presentation-to-application boundary; P2-002 provides presentation primitives without authorization behavior. Locked Technical Architecture requires layered server-side authorization rather than role-only access and treats the browser as untrusted for business authority. Locked relational authority separates User identity from Client/Attorney roles and separates staff identity from Capability Grant authorization, so P2-003 must not collapse principal resolution into a mutable single-role flag. Existing P0 web-application controls already permit bounded apps/web paths while protecting package, dependency, workspace, and repository control state, so no additional P0 control extension or dependency is required.
decisions.impact: If later protected and accepted, this registers only the P2-003 Security Shell contract. It does not begin P2-003 application implementation; create authentication or profile workflows; connect Supabase Auth or any other identity provider; read or mutate database state; change SQL, schema, RLS, ACLs, Storage, migrations, providers, packages, lockfiles, workspace configuration, .replit, or CI; create feature-specific routes or business authorization; classify or activate Arizona; alter P1-012; resolve F-01/F-02/F-03; touch Staging, Production, or OLD; or authorize any later lifecycle gate.
